theme: Road travel and fuel: gas prices (EIA, AAA), vehicle miles travelled, holiday driving, toll data
queries_run: gh search repos "gas prices eia weekly" --sort stars
gh search repos "vehicle miles traveled" --sort stars
gh search repos "eia gas prices python" --sort updated
gh search repos "aaa gas prices" --sort stars
gh search repos "eia api energy data" --sort stars

candidates.name: py-gasbuddy
candidates.what_it_holds: Python library (18 stars, updated 7 Sep 2026, MIT) that queries GasBuddy's GraphQL API for station-level fuel prices by station ID, zip, or city; returns current regular/mid/premium/diesel price and station metadata. No historical data committed — a live pull method only.
candidates.why_useful: GasBuddy crowd-sourced gas prices are a leading, high-frequency (sub-daily) proxy for road-trip cost, which is the key substitute-cost driver for domestic drive-to leisure travel (gap #10, road/fuel theme); pairing weekly national averages with holiday-driving forecasts could feed a NA leisure-demand nowcast alongside TSA and nights data. Would need a scheduled pull to build a point-in-time series from today forward; no backfill.

candidates.name: ha-gasbuddy
candidates.what_it_holds: Home Assistant integration (65 stars, updated 11 Sep 2026, MIT) wrapping py-gasbuddy to poll a single station's price on a schedule and expose it as a smart-home sensor.
candidates.why_useful: Same underlying GasBuddy data as py-gasbuddy but wired for scheduled polling/logging, which is closer to a ready-made point-in-time capture harness (poll daily, log to CSV) than the bare library is; still single-station granularity, needs adaptation for national/regional averages.

candidates.name: aaa_gas_scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Small scraper (updated 13 Sep 2026, actively run 'once a day') pulling AAA's published gas-price pages for Nevada, Las Vegas, and Reno specifically. Repo appears to be actively logging daily runs (very recent update).
candidates.why_useful: AAA's daily national/state/city average gas price feed (the standard press benchmark cited around holiday-driving forecasts) is not otherwise in our catalogue; this shows AAA's page is scrape-able and gives a working pattern, though scope is limited to 3 Nevada geographies. A generalized version (all 50 states) would be more useful than this one.
candidates.time_coverage: ongoing daily since unknown start, small n likely
candidates.size_hint: small scraper + presumably a growing local log (not confirmed committed)

candidates.name: Vehicle-miles-traveled-by-state
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed dataset stitching together FHWA (Federal Highway Administration) Traffic Volume Trends monthly state-level VMT spreadsheets into one file, built by a data journalism shop (TrendCT); one row/file per state per month, sourced directly from FHWA's monthly reports.
candidates.why_useful: State-level monthly VMT is a direct measure of US road-travel volume and a plausible complement to TSA throughput (already held, flagged as not working post-2024) for the domestic drive-market share of leisure travel; state granularity could support a NA-region driving-vs-flying mix proxy for gap #10.
candidates.time_coverage: FHWA monthly VMT series through ~2021 (repo stale since)
candidates.size_hint: small, stitched CSV(s) from monthly FHWA spreadsheets

candidates.name: Time-Series-VMT-Analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed monthly US national Vehicle Miles Traveled series 1972-2008 (likely sourced from FHWA), used for a time-series class analysis notebook/report.
candidates.why_useful: Long back-history (36 years) of national VMT could help establish seasonal/holiday-driving baselines and cyclical patterns predating the FHWA data our other candidate (trendct) covers only recently; useful mainly as a historical reference series, not current.

candidates.name: COVID---19-Travel-Data
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed combined dataset: monthly TSA passenger throughput, monthly state-level VMT, quarterly average domestic airline itinerary fares by state, and monthly COVID-19 cases/deaths by state, built to compare air vs. road travel during the pandemic.
candidates.why_useful: Joins VMT with TSA throughput and airfares in one panel, which is a ready-made air-vs-road substitution frame; however TSA-post-2024 already failed as a nowcast per our own tests, and this data appears COVID-era vintage (2020-21), so its marginal value is mainly the joined structure/methodology rather than fresh numbers.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps TSA throughput (already held) and VMT-by-state (candidate above)

candidates.name: AAA-Gas-Prices-Module
candidates.what_it_holds: Discord bot module (0 stars, last updated Feb 2024) that scrapes AAA's gas-price website on command; no data committed, method only.
candidates.why_useful: Second confirmation that AAA's national/state gas-price page is scrape-able; low value beyond that since it stores nothing and is unmaintained.

candidates.name: gasbuddy-mcp-price-tracker
candidates.what_it_holds: An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server (1 star, updated 22 Apr 2026, MIT) that lets an LLM tool-call gasbuddy.com for cheapest station prices by city/zip; no stored data.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal: shows another live-query path into GasBuddy but adds nothing over py-gasbuddy for building a time series; flagged mainly for completeness under 'methods/tooling'.

notes: EIA-specific searches ('gas prices eia weekly', 'eia api energy data') returned zero gh search hits — no committed EIA weekly retail gasoline price mirrors or maintained EIA API client repos surfaced under those terms; worth a follow-up with different phrasing ('eia-python', 'pyeia', 'EIA-data-scraper') if another scout has search budget. Toll data (E-ZPass, turnpike traffic) and holiday-driving-forecast-specific repos were not reached: the gh search budget (6 calls) was spent on gas-price/VMT terms first, and the WebSearch tool then reported its session-wide budget (200/200) was already exhausted by other concurrent scouts before I could run toll-data or holiday-driving queries — those sub-areas of this theme are effectively unscouted and should be retried by another agent with a fresh search budget. Overall this theme is thin on GitHub: gas-price data lives mostly behind live scraper/API-wrapper repos (GasBuddy, AAA) with no historical series committed, and VMT has one usable stitched FHWA dataset (trendct) plus one long-history academic one (1972-2008); nothing found beats or extends what's already flagged as not working (TSA post-2024).
